sections.title: Measurement outcomes and the Born rule
sections.question: How does a declared projective measurement map a normalized state to probabilities for classical outcome labels?
sections.exit: StatefiniteprojectiveBornruleaspostulate;derivepositivity andnormalization;translatecomputational labels,marginals andcoarse outcomes without confusingprobabilities withsamples orstateupdates.

sections.title: Conditional states and ignored outcomes
sections.question: Given a declared ideal projective update, what state is assigned to a selected nonzero branch, and how are later probabilities computed when its outcome is ignored?
sections.entry: 6.1 pure global states, orthogonal complete projectors and Born probabilities; normalized conditional vector is an additional ideal-update assumption.
sections.exit: Prove branch normalization, repeatability, ordered sequential joint and ignored-outcome marginal probabilities; distinguish coarse projection from fine measurement with a forgotten record, without averaging vectors.
sections.worked_case: Complex qubit; ordered register masks; Bell correlations; Z-then-plus interference; parity-versus-fine within-event coherence.
sections.boundary: Pure global inputs and finite projectors; branch enumeration is classical postprocessing of an actual simulated preparation. No native collapse or shots, no mixed-state operator update before Chapter 8.
sections.code_plan: Use released native FQ preparation and exact computational probability queries; explicit branch/joint helpers with zero/rare-event contracts.
sections.independent_check: Scalar coordinate masks, closed phase formulas, independently indexed prepared states and unnormalized ordered projector products.
sections.transfer_task: New nonadjacent four-qubit selections and complex Fourier rank-two projections.

sections.title: Observables, spectra, and expectations
sections.question: How do real spectral outcome values and Born probabilities produce an expectation, and how does that identity map to native FlagQuantum observables?
sections.entry: 6.1 complete projective probabilities; 2.5 finite Hermitian spectral theorem and degenerate subspaces.
sections.exit: Prove the weighted-spectral/quadratic identity, reality, spectral bounds and real linearity; distinguish outcome, expectation, correlated product and measurement protocol.
sections.worked_case: Z readout; complex Pauli-Y signs; tilted H; degenerate ZZ; reversed nonadjacent Pauli support; noncommuting sum and affine units.
sections.boundary: Finite normalized pure inputs and Hermitian observables; native real Pauli sums, explicit classical spectra. No general hardware readout protocol, variance/shot statistics or mixed-state expectations.
sections.code_plan: Actual fq.expectation named requests and result.expectation; @ on disjoint observables, * real scalar; dense and explicit-projector checks.
sections.independent_check: Closed one-qubit amplitudes/means and analytic H projectors; scalar parity sums; indexed preparations and numerical spectral reconstructions.
sections.transfer_task: New complex Hermitian two-qubit Pauli sum and reversed nonadjacent four-qubit support.

sections.title: Measuring in another basis
sections.question: Which actual pre-readout circuit implements a declared projective basis, and how do its labels relate to the original state?
sections.entry: 3.5 basis conjugation; 5.1 chronological composition and inversion; 6.3 projectors and spectral weights.
sections.exit: Prove R-dagger Q R effective projectors and B-dagger analyzers, derive X/Y and tilted circuits, handle partial ordered readout, entangled bases and label/phase conventions.
sections.worked_case: X: H; Y: P(-pi/2) then H; tilted Rz/Ry inverse order; ordered local Y/X on correlated register; Bell analyzer.
sections.boundary: Ideal unitary rotations before native exact computational probability queries. No native arbitrary-projector request, shots, noisy measurement calibration or collapsed-state claim.
sections.code_plan: Execute actual named rotations and CNOT analyzers; custom unitary only for explicit column-phase/permutation diagnostics with book unitary guard.
sections.independent_check: Explicit conjugated projectors, scalar column overlaps, indexed prepared/rotated vectors and closed Pauli sign tests.
sections.transfer_task: Fresh tilted angles and new four-qubit ordered partial support.

sections.title: Generalized measurements and instruments [Advanced]
sections.question: What do POVM effects determine, what extra update information do measurement operators supply, and which operational information belongs to an instrument?
sections.entry: 6.1 Born probabilities; 6.2 pure global branches and probability sums; 2.4 adjoints/isometries.
sections.exit: State generalized measurement postulates, derive pure-input normalization/update consistency, distinguish effects from different instrument updates and nonunique hidden operator representations.
sections.worked_case: Weak Z effects with diagonal measurement operators versus outcome-conditioned X; native controlled-meter rotations; genuine trine POVM; coarse hidden branches and representation mixing.
sections.boundary: Pure inputs and branch ensembles; full mixed-input instrument maps/composition remain in 9.7 and density-state formalism in Chapter 8. Native unitary dilation and computational probabilities, no invented POVM/collapse API.
sections.code_plan: Native Ry/CRy/CX with a zero meter, exact meter readout; original classical effect/operator-group validators and branch enumeration; trine predictions on real native preparations.
sections.independent_check: Explicit joint amplitude blocks, scalar weak/trine probabilities, later-event sums and alternate hidden representations.
sections.transfer_task: Fresh strengths/complex inputs and new trine preparations.
